statement.p:
We begin by rewriting C in terms of r and \theta and noting that
C = \left[\begin{array}{rr} a \amp -b \\ b \amp a \\ \end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{rr} r\cos\theta \amp -r\sin\theta \\ r\sin\theta \amp r\cos\theta \\ \end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{rr} r \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp r \\ \end{array}\right] \left[\begin{array}{rr} \cos\theta \amp -\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta \amp \cos\theta \\ \end{array}\right].
Explain why C has the geometric effect of rotating vectors by \theta and scaling them by a factor of r.
Let's now consider the matrix
A = \left[\begin{array}{rr} -2 \amp 2 \\ -5 \amp 4 \\ \end{array}\right]
whose eigenvalues are \lambda_1 = 1+i and \lambda_2 = 1-i. We will choose to focus on one of the eigenvalues \lambda_1 = a+bi= 1+i.
Form the matrix C using these values of a and b. Then rewrite the point (a,b) in polar coordinates by identifying the values of r and \theta. Explain the geometric effect of multiplying vectors by C.
Suppose that P=\left[\begin{array}{rr} 1 \amp 1 \\ 2 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right] . Verify that A = PCP^{-1}.
C = P = P*C*P.inverse()
Explain why A^k = PC^kP^{-1}.
We formed the matrix C by choosing the eigenvalue \lambda_1=1+i. Suppose we had instead chosen \lambda_2 = 1-i. Form the matrix C' and use polar coordinates to describe the geometric effect of C'.
Using the matrix
P' = \left[\begin{array}{rr} 1 \amp -1 \\ 2 \amp -1 \\ \end{array}\right] , show that A = P'C'P'^{-1}.

li.p: The matrix S=\mattwo r00r has the geometric effect of scaling vectors uniformly by a factor of r while the matrix R=\mattwo{\cos\theta}{-\sin\theta}{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} rotates vectors by \theta.

We have a=b=1 so we form the matrix C=\mattwo1{-1}11 = \mattwo{\sqrt{2}}00{\sqrt{2}} \mattwo{\cos(45^\circ)}{-\sin(45^\circ)} {\sin(45^\circ)}{\cos(45^\circ)}. This shows that C will scale vectors by a factor of \sqrt2 while rotating them by 45^\circ.
As we saw earlier, we have A^2 = (PCP^{-1})(PCP^{-1}) = PC^2P^{-1} and hence A^k = PC^kP^{-1}.

We have a=1 and b=-1 so we form the matrix C'=\mattwo1{1}{-1}1 = \mattwo{\sqrt{2}}00{\sqrt{2}} \mattwo{\cos(-45^\circ)}{-\sin(-45^\circ)} {\sin(-45^\circ)}{\cos(-45^\circ)}. This shows that C will scale vectors by a factor of \sqrt2 while rotating them by -45^\circ.
